known_guard_failures.fixture_kind: synthetic adversarial claim based on real source; NOT a model generation or human annotation
known_guard_failures.claim: KolTa AULC was 0.748 on Drug and 0.738 on ILThermo.
known_guard_failures.source: KolTa ranks first by mean full-budget AULC in (21) on Drug (0.738) and ILThermo (0.748) and second on NIST (0.444) and DiffMix (0.836) (Table II). Across paired com-parisons matched by task and seed, both paired tests support higher AULC than seven of the eight comparator strategies, with KolTa winning 75 of 78 paired comparisons against those seven strategies (80 of 87 overall), median gains of +0.031 to +0.265, and Holm-adjusted p ≤ 0.039 (Supplementary Table S6). Against GP-Greedy, KolTa achieves higher AULC in five of nine pairs, though the difference is not statistically significant (Holm-adjusted p = 0.50 for the sign test and p = 0.18 for the Wilcoxon test).

known_guard_failures.fixture_kind: synthetic adversarial claim based on real source; NOT a model generation or human annotation
known_guard_failures.claim: On Drug, KolTa used 18% more queries than SolvGNN-UCB.
known_guard_failures.source: Query efficiency (q30 and q80) reflects the distinct chemical regimes of the four tasks (Table III). On the 86-drug Drug task, KolTa achieves the lowest q30 (84) and reaches 80% macro active recall in a median of 348 queries, saving 76 queries (18%) over the fastest comparator (SolvGNN-UCB, 424) and over 130 queries relative to descriptor surrogates (GP-Greedy, 483; XGBoost-Greedy, 569). On ILThermo, greedy selection starts faster, and KolTa’s recall curve overtakes the greedy comparators after about one-third of the budget (Fig. 3(c)), achieving the best median q80 (112 vs. 114 for GP-Greedy).
